ListItems.Title: Crocodile Museum
ListItems.Description:
The Crocodile Museum is located next to the Kom Ombo temple, north of Aswan. This museum has highlighted the crocodile-headed god Sobek since it was opened in 2012. Its main exhibition hall displays the mummified mummies of Nile crocodiles. The longest crocodile was 4.30 m, while the smallest was 2 m.

ListItems.Title: The work of the Egyptian archaeological mission in Wadi Abu Saubeira
ListItems.Description: The work of the Egyptian archaeological mission in Wadi Abu Subeira in the Eastern desert northeast of Aswan, uncovered a series of royal rock inscriptions. Dating back to the end of the Neolithic period, the inscriptions depict Egyptian royal symbols, along with many animals such as giraffes, elephants and crocodiles The work of the Egyptian archaeological mission in Wadi Abu Subeira

ListItems.Title: Mummification Museum
ListItems.Description:
Mummification museum in Luxor (ancient Thebes), intended to provide an understanding of the process to preserve the body. The ancient Egyptians not only applied embalming to dead humans but also to many animals (Cats, dogs, crocodiles…. etc.). God Anubis(the Jackal) was the god of embalming and mummification.

ListItems.Title: A new archaeological discovery at Tell el-Faraoun in Sharqia Governorate
ListItems.Description:
The ruins of city "Emet" were found in Tell el-Faraoun (Tell Nabasha) area in Husseiniya Center in Sharqia Governorate, at conclusion of the current excavation season, which was carried out by British archaeological mission from University of Manchester.

ListItems.Title: New Discoveries at Saqqara
ListItems.Description: H.E. The Minister of Antiquities, Dr. Khaled El-Enany, announced on Saturday at an international press conference a new archaeological discovery in Saqqara. The discovery was carried out by an Egyptian archaeological mission, headed by Dr. Mostafa Waziri, Secretary General of the Supreme Council of Antiquities, during its work at the animal cemetery.
